correctness.rationale: The affine curve v³+At⁶+B=0 has six simple finite branch points of a separable degree-three covering, unramified infinity, and genus four by Riemann-Hurwitz. The sextic Fermat curve maps via squared coordinates to the untwisted canonical model and is itself a quotient of a Hermitian maximal curve because 6 divides p+1. Consequently Frobenius on H¹ of the base model is scalar −p. Its eight tame character weights (2,1),(1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(1,5),(2,5),(2,4),(2,3) couple to descent exponents (2si−rj mod6). Pairing their conjugates gives the four cyclotomic factors with eight distinct signature classes on the exact 18 coefficient types. Independently enumerated all 18 characters and reproduced multiplicities 1,2,4,2,4,2,1,2 for the eight signatures, independently of the source’s finite-field verifier. The argument, not finite p=5,11,17 examples, establishes every allowed p.
residual_risks: p must be prime p≡5(mod6), p>=5; q=p²; coefficients A,B nonzero; all results concern the displayed diagonal affine equivalence, not the moduli of all genus-four curves.
Character-sign conventions must be applied consistently; the independent finite signature check is not a second proof of supersingularity/maximality for every prime.
